why: The answer turns the switch into one else-if chain: case 1 becomes the first test, the fall-through cases 2 and 3 are joined with ||, and default becomes the final else, but it writes the Python keyword 'elif' instead of Java's 'else if', so it does not compile and is a relational answer with an error. The run facts only check value 1, so they do not show the chain's logic is wrong.

concepts.quote: if (value == 1) result = 30; elif (value == 2 || value == 3) result = -10; else result = 5;
concepts.why: It builds a correct else-if chain whose final else catches the default case, but 'elif' is not Java and must be 'else if'.
The first test is a correctly written Java if with a boolean condition and a single-statement body, but the answer does not trace or explain it.
It joins two comparisons with || into one boolean condition, which matches the fall-through of case 2 into case 3.
The answer makes no claim about which operand of || gets evaluated.
